response.title: Binary search
response.question_prompt: Explain how binary search finds a value in a list. Say why the list must be sorted, how the search range changes at each step, when the search stops, and how fast it is.
response.answer_text: Binary search only works on a sorted list. It looks at the middle element and compares it with the target. If the target is bigger it throws away the left half, otherwise the right half. It keeps halving until it finds the value or there is nothing left, so it takes about log n steps.
response.trap_explanation: The student rejected the claim that binary search works on unsorted lists and explained that order is what lets it discard half.
response.weakest_key_point: It is much faster than linear search on large lists, which checks every element.

key_points.statement: The list must be sorted, because each comparison relies on order to rule out half the list.
key_points.comment: Covered clearly, including why order matters.
key_points.evidence_quote: Binary search only works on a sorted list, because if it isn't sorted throwing away half could throw away the target.

key_points.statement: Each step compares the target with the middle element of the current range.
key_points.evidence_quote: It looks at the middle element and compares it with the target.

key_points.statement: The range shrinks by moving the low or high bound past the middle, discarding the half that cannot hold the target.
key_points.comment: Partly covered. Describe how the low and high bounds move.
key_points.evidence_quote: If the target is bigger it throws away the left half, otherwise the right half.

key_points.statement: The search stops when the target is found, or when the range is empty (low passes high) and it reports not found.
key_points.comment: Partly covered. Explain both ways the search can end.
key_points.evidence_quote: It keeps halving until it finds the value or there is nothing left.

key_points.statement: It runs in O(log n) time because the range halves at every step.
key_points.evidence_quote: It keeps halving until it finds the value or there is nothing left, so it takes about log n steps.
